raw_response:
I farm only 3 mu, so I cannot take big risks. What I do is mostly based on what has worked on my own land and what other people around the village are doing. I finished middle school, so I do listen when the extension people talk about split fertilizer and timing, but in the end I still decide by looking at the field. For my wheat-maize land, I will keep the full 3 mu in the same double-cropping pattern. Wheat and maize both give me steady grain, and with such a small area I care more about stable harvest than trying something fancy.

For wheat, I will sow in early October, not too late, because late wheat in our place usually does poorly. I will use a common improved variety that is easy to buy locally, put on base fertilizer before sowing, and then topdress once around jointing if the seedlings look strong enough to support it. I have a well, so I will irrigate wheat about three times, but I will watch the pumping cost and skip one round if spring rain is decent. After wheat harvest in June, I will move fast into summer maize because that turnaround is always tight here. For maize I will use hybrid seed, do simple rotary tillage or direct planting right after wheat if I can get help in time, and apply most fertilizer early with one topdress at the big bell stage. I will irrigate maize once if the soil is dry after emergence or around tasseling. I do not want to underfeed the crop, but I also cannot spend too much cash on only 3 mu, so I will stay with a moderate input level, close to what has given me decent yields before.
